findings: The complete source gives Baird’s seven-state/two-action example: gamma=.99, zero rewards, dashed/solid behavior probabilities 6/7 and 1/7, solid target policy, exact eight-dimensional state features, and initial vector (1,1,1,1,1,1,10,1). It says semi-gradient TD(0) diverges for every positive step size and includes the expected DP-update divergence plot; the scaffold carefully does not upgrade this to a sample-path almost-sure theorem.

Sutton–Barto §11.6 explicitly constructs two MRPs with the same observable feature/reward sequence distribution but different Bellman-error objective values and different minimizers. MRPs have no action-dependent policy, so this source example is now separated from ML-79’s offline unseen-action MDP impossibility.
The source examples do not establish universal divergence for all approximators or deep RL; the exact finite matrix calculation and local proof remain to be written.

findings: Sutton’s Dyna-Q description uses a deterministic table model and samples only experienced state-action pairs; it is algorithmic context rather than a stochastic model-accuracy theorem.

Sutton’s almost-sure RTDP result is restricted to undiscounted episodic stochastic optimal-path tasks with absorbing zero-reward goals, a proper policy, strictly negative nonggoal rewards, admissible initial values, and its stated greedy/start-state conditions. The edited plan carries these premises.

A local finite-horizon bound is proposed only for one fixed policy, common initial law, rewards in [0,1], uniform reward error, and TV transition error over the union of reachable pairs. The bound’s proof is local; it does not control an optimizer selected in the learned model or unsupported states.

findings: Levine et al. is a full tutorial/review, not a proof source for the proposed doubly robust estimator or local support-impossibility construction. It presents trajectory importance sampling, per-decision and weighted estimators, and doubly robust OPE while attributing formal details to cited papers.

The scoped unbiasedness argument now requires target trajectory-law absolute continuity, correct behavior ratios, finite-horizon integrability, and an explicit dataset sampling model. Doubly robust alternatives must be proved separately: correct propensities, or a correct finite-horizon value model including the terminal convention.
The observation-equivalent offline example uses two finite MDPs agreeing on the logged behavior support but differing on an unseen target action; it is distinct from ML-77’s action-free pair of MRPs.

findings: The full Brown report is the source for finite known-model POMDP semantics, belief update and sufficient-statistic reduction, finite policy trees, alpha-vector linear values, piecewise-linear convex finite-horizon values, and witness backups/pruning.

The finite Bayes formula requires positive observation probability for the realized observation; zero-probability observations are null under the model and need only a filler if the update is defined everywhere.
The report is not a model-learning result and notes policy-tree/witness growth; infinite-horizon discounted values may need infinitely many facets, so the finite-horizon statement is retained.
